clues: This city sits in the southwest of a country in Africa. It stands on the Chari River, not far from Lake Chad.
This place has a hot, dry climate with one clear dry season each year. The river gives water for farms and homes, but the flat land around it stays dry.
French rulers founded this city in 1910 when they held this part of Africa. It got a new local name in 1975 to show its own roots.
Two big rivers meet here, and a town in the next country sits just across the water. This port town is a key crossroads for trade in the whole region.
This is Chad's capital, its seat of rule. It is the biggest city in the whole land too.
